newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices on Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower on continued thin packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Demand was seen light through the weekend as many packers continued to fight unprofitable operating margins by reducing operating schedules.
At least one major hog plant in the eastern Corn Belt that usually slaughters on Saturday reportedly will take this weekend off, hog buyers there said.
Hog numbers were drifting lower following a midweek bulge when farmers sold animals held back during recent fieldwork.
Rain Wednesday into Thursday soaked fields in Iowa and stalled corn planting, which allowed farmers a chance to catch up on their hog marketings.
But the tighter late-week supplies could curb hog price declines, some sources noted.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Wednesday were 110,000 head, above the estimate of 105,000, USDA statistics showed. Thursday's estimate was 105,000 head.
Top cash prices for hogs delivered to plants in interior Iowa/southern Minnesota Friday could range $58.00 to $58.50.
Illinois tops at plants could range $57.00 to $57.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could span $57.00 to $57.50.
